clue.text: Make poor little devil the surplus one at whist

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
over means left over, in excess
I is the Roman numeral one
whist is an old interjection calling for silence, like sh

explanation.surface: A card player complains about the useless spare man at a game of whist.
explanation.walkthrough: Whist looks like the card game, but here it is the old word meaning 'hush!'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impoverish someone is to reduce them to poverty.

clue.text: The girl-is hot and in a temper

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A girl who is hot-tempered and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get one's Irish up' means to lose one's temper, so Irish can mean temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is a colloquial word for anger, as in getting someone's Irish up.

clue.text: Ate out

parts.note: eating out usually means at a restaurant, but here it means a meal taken outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: To picnic is to eat a meal in the open air.

clue.text: It put a very vile version in an abusive way

indicators.note: a version is one rendering of something, so the letters appear in a new form

explanation.surface: A nasty rendering phrased offensively.
explanation.definitionFit: Vituperatively means with harsh, insulting language.

clue.text: Get in line again for relief

definitions.meaning: to dress ranks is to line soldiers up
relief or remedy for a wrong

explanation.surface: Soldiers form up once more to be relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing ranks aligns troops, done again here; and redress is compensation that relieves a grievance.

clue.text: Not shiny like the sea in Xanadu

definitions.meaning: Coleridge's Kubla Khan describes a river running down to a sea without sunlight

explanation.surface: Coleridge's dark sea, by the pleasure dome.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking sunshine is gloomy; and Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan describes the sea at Xanadu with this word.

clue.text: One in a hundred thousand of the people

indicators.note: the word in tells us the one is placed inside the hundred thousand

parts.note: a lac (lakh) is the Indian word for a hundred thousand
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rare person, one in a hundred thousand of the population.
explanation.walkthrough: LAC, or lakh, is the South Asian term for 100,000, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay, belonging to the ordinary people rather than the clergy.

clue.text: A Slav sounds bitter

indicators.note: sounds means the words are spoken and spelt differently

parts.note: a Serb is a Slav from Serbia, preceded by a

explanation.surface: A Slavic man has a sour voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a variant of acerbic, meaning sour or sharp.

clue.text: Several studies by journalist boiled down

parts.note: to con is to study, and dens are studies, rooms for private work
dens are studies, quiet rooms
ED, editor, is the crossword's journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist's many research reports, all summarised.
explanation.walkthrough: Two kinds of study: CON (to study) and DENS (studies as rooms).
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed means shortened or concentrated, reduced to essentials.

clue.text: Rump polished off at end of this protracted diet

definitions.text: Rump polished off at end of this protracted diet

parts.words: Rump polished off at end of this protracted diet
parts.note: a diet is an assembly; the Rump was what remained of a lengthy English assembly of 1640 to 1660

explanation.surface: Someone loses their backside fat at the end of a long diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' means an assembly, not slimming. Purged in 1648, this body left a Rump that was dissolved in 1653.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliament summoned by Charles I in 1640 sat, in remnant form as the Rump, until 1660, hence its name.

clue.text: Encouraged sound understanding with daughter

indicators.note: sound here means the word is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: insight is deep understanding

explanation.surface: A parent praised for raising a daughter with good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound understanding' reads as an adjective and noun, but 'sound' signals a homophone: INSIGHT is heard as INCITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite someone is to urge or stir them on.

clue.text: Kind of stone to get water from?

definitions.text: Kind of stone to get water from?

parts.words: Kind of stone to get water from?
parts.note: in Greek myth a grieving mother was turned to stone that wept forever, so this stone yields tears, not water from a spring

explanation.surface: A question about a rock that holds a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Niobe, mourning her slain children, was turned to a stone that still weeps; the adjective from her name describes such tearful stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the weeping mother of myth, endlessly tearful as a rock running with water.

clue.text: A transformation to shock a bit

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it
a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: A sudden change that comes as something of a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformation' is an old trade name for a wig or false hair, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A transformation was a dated term for a wig or false hair worn to change one's look.

clue.text: It's a gift to the French film star

parts.note: the gift of the gab is talkativeness, so gab is a gift
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone presents a gift to a celebrated French actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Gable was the Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a leading Hollywood actor of the 1930s to 1950s.

clue.text: Speaker left off the receiver

indicators.note: off tells us the letter for left is dropped from the speaker

parts.note: a talker is one who speaks

explanation.surface: Someone talking puts the telephone handset down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a phone handset, but it means the person who receives or takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A taker is one who accepts or receives something offered.

clue.text: Nude torso concealed around course

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A naked body hidden beneath a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concealed' adds to the picture of a covered torso; 'around' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos is a small round fillet steak served as a main course.

clue.text: As far as possible, afloat in a bark

indicators.note: in places the shipboard letters inside the rearranged words
possible suggests the words could be arranged another way

parts.note: SS (steamship) stands for being on a vessel, afloat

explanation.surface: Drifting as far as one can in a small sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' suggests a sailing ship (barque), but it is tree bark. 'Possible' rearranges AS FAR AS into SAAFRAS, and 'in' puts SS inside it after SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassafras is a North American tree whose aromatic root bark is used for flavouring.

clue.text: Creeping inertia — record chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A slow inertia overtaking a disorderly record collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptiles crawl, so reptilian can mean creeping or grovelling.

clue.text: A Foreign Office sounding almost entirely disobedient

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: sounding says the word for office is taken by ear, so spelt another way

parts.note: an office is a duty or charge

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut

parts.note: full means entirely, as in full well

explanation.surface: A Foreign Office described as nearly completely unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounding' lets DUTY be heard as DUTI; 'almost' cuts the last L from FULL to give FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undutiful fails in their obligations, and so is not obedient.

clue.text: Waste fried food

explanation.surface: Squandering money on fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter away time is to squander it; and a fritter is fruit or meat dipped in batter and fried.

clue.text: A sign to the Muses of Latin verse

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
there were nine Muses

explanation.surface: Astrology and the Muses inspire a Latin poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine verse is a medieval Latin metre with internal rhyme.

clue.text: Fat for making cover round pastry, one might say

indicators.note: round tells us the cover goes around the next piece

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: one might say signals that the word is spoken, so spelt differently

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A recipe uses fat to make a crust over a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One might say' turns PIE into its sound-alike PI, which goes inside LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipids are the chemical class of fats and oils.

clue.text: Parts of Geneva without a Jewish area

indicators.note: parts of suggests the city's letters are broken up and rearranged, once the a is taken away

explanation.surface: Bits of Geneva lacking a Jewish quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a' removes A from GENEVA, leaving GENEV, which 'Parts of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the desert region of southern Israel.

clue.text: Porridge as a punishment

definitions.meaning: to give someone ... is an old phrase for punishing them severely

explanation.surface: Prison porridge served up as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, porridge also means a prison sentence, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruel is a thin oat porridge; and taking one's gruel meant receiving harsh punishment.

clue.text: One answer would, be a U-turn in this segregation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letter U turns into an a, swapped in its place

parts.note: a solution is an answer

explanation.surface: One answer would be to reverse this policy of segregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U-turn' reads as a reversal, but it means the U turns into 'a': SOLUTION becomes SOLATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is the state of being kept apart from others.

clue.text: They get a bashing that serves' them right in Scotland

definitions.text: They get a bashing that serves' them right in Scotland

parts.words: They get a bashing that serves' them right in Scotland
parts.note: in Scotland swede turnips are mashed, bashed, and served with haggis

explanation.surface: Rough justice for wrongdoers north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bashed' is the Scottish word for mashed root vegetables served with haggis.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps are Scots for turnips or swedes, mashed to go with haggis.

clue.text: There are clearly two t's in attire

parts.note: double means two of something
the letter t, of which two are wanted

explanation.surface: An observation that a word for clothing obviously has a pair of t's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two t's' is read as 'double T'. A doublet is a close-fitting jacket of Tudor times.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a man's close-fitting jacket worn in the 15th to 17th centuries.

clue.text: The article is an eye-opener: make a note of it

parts.note: an item is an article, a single thing
taken as written

indicators.note: an opener is what starts something, so the first letter of eye

explanation.surface: A magazine piece proves revealing and worth recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-opener' looks like a revelation, but it is the first letter of 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list things one by one, noting each down.

clue.text: Scotsman leaves the sage alone

indicators.note: leaves means the Scotsman goes out of the sage's name

parts.note: King Solomon is the proverbial wise man
mon is a jocular Scottish form of man

explanation.surface: A Scotsman walks out and leaves the wise man by himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo means done by oneself, without others.

clue.text: S Americans entering as cooks

indicators.note: cooks means the letters are worked over and reorganised

explanation.surface: South Americans coming in to work as cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' looks like a noun naming the job, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentines are people of Argentina, in South America.
